BiblicalUsage: Adrazda is an Aramaic adverb meaning diligently, exactly, with care — and it appears only once, in King Artaxerxes' letter to Ezra: whatever the God of heaven commands 'shall be done diligently' for His house. The Persian king, who did not know this God, still ordered that His temple be supplied without delay and without excuse.
TheologicalSignificance: There is no creed in this word, only a clear meaning in context, and I am content to leave the theology to the verse around it; in this case, the verse is Ezra 7:23.
